operations.specification: Implement POST /auth/guest/join as guest registration/auth initialization that creates a member-like authentication context for a guest to receive tokens. Parse JSON body according to IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IJoin. Validate required fields (e.g., email/password) using service-layer rules defined in the auth analysis; reject invalid input with 400. On success, create or locate guest-related identity record in erp_hrm_time_tracking_guests (and corresponding session artifacts if required by schema) and issue JWT access/refresh tokens embedded in the returned IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IAuthorized. Persist any refresh-token/session mapping to erp_hrm_time_tracking_guest_sessions when applicable, within a transaction. Ensure rate-limiting / throttling hook points exist for security. Return 201 with IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IAuthorized on success. Return 409 for already-used identifiers when applicable; otherwise 401/403 for credential or verification failures. Ensure no cross-organization data reads occur for guest.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows an unauthenticated guest actor to start the authentication workflow and obtain the tokens required for subsequent authenticated interactions.

It is explicitly scoped to the guest actor by authorizationActor='guest' and is the only guest authentication entry point besides token renewal. The implementation must accept the request payload described by the required DTO type IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IJoin and return an authorization result described by IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IAuthorized.

Service-layer behavior should create (or correlate) the guest identity in the guest actor tables (see erp_hrm_time_tracking_guests) and persist any guest-session linkage in the guest session table (erp_hrm_time_tracking_guest_sessions) so that refresh can later validate and re-issue tokens. If the join flow includes email/password credential checks, password verification must occur before issuing tokens.

Security considerations: never return sensitive credential material, never include password-reset or verification tokens in the success payload, and ensure token issuance is performed only after validation passes. Errors should be consistent and avoid leaking which part of the credentials was incorrect.

Related operations: clients should call POST /auth/guest/refresh when the issued access token expires, using the refresh token included in IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IAuthorized.

requestBody.description: Guest join / sign-in bootstrap payload used to validate credentials and establish a guest authentication session.

responseBody.description: Tokens and authorization state for the guest actor after a successful join flow.

operations.name: joinGuest

operations.specification:
Implement POST /auth/guest/refresh as token renewal for guest actor. Parse JSON body according to IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IRefresh. Validate the refresh token signature and expiry. Look up the guest session record in erp_hrm_time_tracking_guest_sessions and ensure it is associated with the correct guest identity in erp_hrm_time_tracking_guests. If schema supports rotation, revoke/replace the old refresh token mapping atomically in a transaction. Issue a new access token and (if required by DTO) a new refresh token, returning IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IAuthorized.

On invalid/expired refresh tokens, return 401 Unauthorized. On mismatched session/guest identity, return 403 Forbidden. Ensure idempotency where possible (e.g., if the same refresh token is submitted twice during rotation, second call should fail after revocation).

Return 200 with IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IAuthorized on success.
operations.description:
This endpoint renews guest authentication tokens without requiring the guest to re-submit join credentials.

It is explicitly limited to the guest actor by authorizationActor='guest' and uses the required DTO type IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IRefresh for the request and IErpHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IAuthorized for the response.

Implementation must validate the provided refresh token and map it to a persisted guest session record so that token renewal remains consistent with the server-side session artifacts (erp_hrm_time_tracking_guest_sessions) and the guest identity record (erp_hrm_time_tracking_guests).

Security considerations: treat refresh tokens as secrets; never log raw refresh token values; on failure conditions (expired token, revoked session, signature mismatch), return 401/403 without revealing which validation step failed. If refresh-token rotation is implemented, ensure the old refresh token is invalidated so that replay attempts do not succeed.

Related operations: clients should use the refresh token obtained from the successful response of POST /auth/guest/join and call this endpoint when access tokens expire.

requestBody.description: Guest refresh payload containing the refresh token (and any required context) used for token renewal.

responseBody.description: Newly issued guest tokens and authorization state after refresh.

operations.name: refreshGuest

operations.specification: Implement member registration (join): accept member join payload, validate required fields (email/password and any organization-creation inputs per IErpHrmTimeTrackingMember.IJoin contract), create organization and member/account records in a transaction, persist member email verification token if email verification is supported by the system, create an initial member session, and return authorized tokens encapsulated in IErpHrmTimeTrackingMember.IAuthorized. Handle validation errors (duplicate email, invalid password rules) and map to appropriate error responses. Ensure created records are scoped correctly to the newly created organization context for the member.
operations.description:
This endpoint registers a new authenticated "member" account for the ERP HRM time tracking service.

It is the required "join" authorization operation for the member actor and is responsible for creating the underlying member identity record in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_members` (member accounts) and establishing any required membership/account security state that the member login flow relies on. If the platform issues an email verification token, this operation must persist the token in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_email_verifications` so that the email ownership can be verified before granting broader access.

Implementation must return an `IAuthorized` payload containing the newly issued authorization tokens (encapsulated by the response type `IErpHrmTimeTrackingMember.IAuthorized`). These tokens should be created in the same request flow that establishes authentication readiness for the member, leveraging `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions` to persist the session identifier/metadata used by subsequent authenticated requests.

Security considerations: never return password material; treat email/password with strict validation and normalize email consistently. Ensure that if any step fails (member creation, organization creation, token/session issuance), the operation is rolled back so no orphaned session or verification rows remain.

requestBody.description: Member registration payload used to create a new member account and return authorization tokens.

responseBody.description: Authorized response containing tokens after successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implement member login: accept member login payload, validate credentials against stored member record in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_members`, verify password hash, ensure any required email verification status (if enforced) is satisfied using `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_email_verifications`. On success create/refresh member session in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions`, issue JWT access/refresh tokens, and return them as `IErpHrmTimeTrackingMember.IAuthorized`. On failure return authentication error without revealing whether email exists. Record session metadata and support future revocation/rotation as required by the session table.
operations.description:
This endpoint authenticates an existing "member" account and issues authorization tokens.

As the required "login" authorization operation for the member actor, it validates the supplied credentials using the member account data stored in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_members`. If the service requires verified email before access, the implementation must also check the member’s verification state using records represented by `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_email_verifications` and reject login when the account is not yet eligible.

Upon successful authentication, the operation must create or update a member session record in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions` and return an `IAuthorized` payload containing the issued tokens (type `IErpHrmTimeTrackingMember.IAuthorized`). Those tokens are then used by the client to authenticate subsequent member requests scoped to the selected organization context.

Security considerations: apply constant-time comparisons where applicable for password verification, rate-limit login attempts, and never include sensitive fields (like password hashes) in responses. On invalid credentials, respond with generic authentication failure to avoid user enumeration.

requestBody.description: Member login payload containing credentials (e.g., email and password) used to validate identity.

responseBody.description: Authorized response containing tokens after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implement token refresh: accept refresh token payload, validate refresh token and associated session in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions`, ensure the session is valid/not revoked, issue new access/refresh tokens, and return them as `IErpHrmTimeTrackingMember.IAuthorized`. If refresh is tied to email verification or account status, validate accordingly using member record `erp_hrm_time_tracking_members`. Handle expired/invalid tokens with appropriate unauthorized errors.
operations.description:
This endpoint renews authorization tokens for an authenticated "member".

It is the required "refresh" authorization operation for the member actor, intended for clients that already hold refresh credentials. The implementation must validate the provided refresh token against the session state persisted in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions` to ensure the session is still valid. If the member account is subject to eligibility constraints, confirm the member identity in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_members` remains eligible.

After validation, issue a fresh set of tokens and return them in the `IAuthorized` response structure (`IErpHrmTimeTrackingMember.IAuthorized`). The returned tokens should reflect the current session and support subsequent authentication, while preventing reuse of invalidated refresh credentials.

Security considerations: reject expired or mismatched tokens without disclosing which part failed; optionally rotate refresh tokens if the surrounding system design expects it. Ensure new tokens are generated only after session validation succeeds.

requestBody.description: Token refresh payload containing the refresh credentials used to renew tokens.

responseBody.description: Authorized response containing renewed tokens.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Update the current member session context for subsequent organization-scoped operations.

This endpoint is intended for cases where a client needs to change what the server treats as the active session context while staying authenticated. Because this operation is defined as `PATCH /sessions`, it accepts a JSON request body describing the desired session updates and returns the resulting session state.

The server must apply organization-scoped access enforcement for any later operations. When the user switches organization context, subsequent operations must apply to the newly selected organization context, and access must be denied if the user lacks permissions in the target organization.

Implementation-wise, the operation must be rejected (without partial application) when business constraints prevent the session context change. Rejection must produce a clear, human-readable explanation for what prevented completion and must not create misleading audit/activity side effects for rejected business constraints.

Related operations: After successfully updating session context, clients typically call organization-scoped read/write APIs (for example, project or employee management endpoints) that assume the selected organization context is already applied.
operations.name: updateSessionContext
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the caller and resolve the current session identity.
2. Parse PATCH request body for session update instructions (e.g., organization context selection).
3. Validate that the requested organization context is selectable for the user.
   - If the user does not belong to the requested organization, reject the operation.
4. Apply authorization checks under the selected organization context.
   - If the user lacks required permissions for the requested session context, reject.
5. Persist the session context update atomically in a single transaction.
6. Return the updated session view model.
7. Error handling:
   - For any business-rule rejection, return a rejection outcome with a clear explanation and do not apply partial changes.
   - Unexpected internal failures must not modify session state and must avoid inconsistent activity logging.

Note: If the system represents guest and member sessions in different tables, ensure this operation only targets the authenticated member session model relevant to the authenticated actor.

requestBody.description: Session context update payload. Includes the desired updates that the server should apply to the currently active authenticated session.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific live timer tracking session by its identifier.

This operation reads a single {@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_timer_sessions} record and returns the live tracking context captured at the start of the session, including the selected project, optional selected task, and the running description text. The session also exposes its lifecycle markers such as started_at and (when finished) ended_at, and the is_active flag that indicates whether the session is currently the employee’s running session.

Access is restricted to authenticated members with the ability to view time-tracking data within the currently selected organization context. The system must ensure organization-scoped isolation for timer sessions: even if a user knows a sessionId, the record must only be returned when its organization_id matches the organization context selected by the user. Additionally, if the underlying employee is deactivated, the system must reject the time-tracking request as not allowed for the employee’s current status, without altering any persisted time-tracking data.

The returned record is backed directly by the following database columns in erp_hrm_time_tracking_timer_sessions: id (session identifier), organization_id, employee_id, project_id, task_id (optional), description, started_at, ended_at (nullable), is_active, deleted_at (nullable), and audit timestamps created_at and updated_at.

Related usage: after retrieving the session, clients may use the session data to display live tracking state. Starting, stopping, discarding, or updating timer tracking is handled by other TimerSession operations; this endpoint is strictly for viewing a single session record by id.

Error handling expectations:

- If no timer session exists for the given sessionId in the selected organization context, return an appropriate not-found/denied response.
- If the targeted employee is deactivated, return an error indicating the action is not allowed due to employee status.
- If sessionId is malformed or invalid, return a validation error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Parse path parameter sessionId and validate it is a UUID.
2. Determine the requestor’s current organization context from the authenticated session (organization-scoped access enforcement).
3. Query erp_hrm_time_tracking_timer_sessions by id = sessionId.
4. Apply organization scoping at query time (WHERE organization_id = selectedOrganizationId) so cross-organization reads are impossible.
5. Join/check employee status for employee_id against erp_hrm_time_tracking_members (or the effective employee deactivated state as defined in the system) and enforce the rule that deactivated employees cannot use time-tracking operations.
6. If the timer session exists and the employee is allowed, map the timer-session columns into the response DTO.
7. Return the single timer-session payload.

Edge cases:
- If the timer session exists but organization_id does not match, treat it as not found/denied.
- If the employee is deactivated at processing time, reject the request without changing any timelog/timesheet state.

No transaction is required since this is a read-only endpoint.

responseBody.description: The detailed timer session record identified by sessionId, including live tracking context and timestamps.

parameters.description: Timer session identifier (UUID) of the live tracking session to retrieve.
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
This operation updates or creates guest-session correlation data for an unauthenticated visitor so that subsequent requests to protected endpoints can be gated by a valid guest session record.

When a visitor is a guest, the platform has no authenticated organization context and no organization role; therefore, access must be based solely on an explicitly issued guest identity and its session metadata. The guest session metadata is stored in the guest session table, including client IP address, requested URL (href), HTTP referrer, a creation timestamp, and an explicit expiration timestamp used to invalidate tokens after expiry.

This API operation maps directly to the underlying persistence model:
- Guest identity records are stored in the guest identity table, which includes a unique email and a password hash, plus a deleted_at timestamp that indicates whether the guest identity is considered active.
- Guest session records are stored in the guest sessions table and belong to a guest identity record via erp_hrm_time_tracking_guest_id. Each session row has its own created_at and expired_at so the system can enforce expiration without changing the guest identity.

The request body must provide enough information for the service layer to identify the target guest identity (or create a new one during the guest gating flow) and to record the current connection context (ip/href/referrer) into a new guest session row (or refresh an existing one). The service layer must validate that any referenced guest identity is not marked with deleted_at.

Security and validation expectations:
- The service must record ip, href, and referrer values provided by the caller for auditability and gating.
- The service must set expired_at according to the system’s guest session expiration policy (derived from the current server time) and must ensure created_at reflects the actual insertion time.
- If the guest identity is not valid (e.g., it is marked deleted), the operation must reject the request rather than issuing a new session that would bypass the identity state.

Related operations: this endpoint is designed to be used before protected guest-to-auth transitions and before any endpoint that requires a valid guest session token. The returned payload should be used by the client to attach correlation information to subsequent requests.

Error handling:
- Invalid or missing required request fields must be rejected with a 4xx response.
- If session creation fails due to database constraints or identity state (e.g., deleted identity), the operation must fail without creating a partially inconsistent guest/session record.
operations.name: updateGuestSession
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:
1) Parse request body containing guest identity correlation inputs (e.g., guestEmail) and connection metadata (ip/href/referrer).
2) Look up erp_hrm_time_tracking_guests by unique email.
   - If a record exists and deleted_at is null, treat it as active.
   - If it exists but deleted_at is non-null, reject (do not issue sessions for deleted identities).
   - If no record exists, create a new erp_hrm_time_tracking_guests row.
     - For creation, set email and password_hash from the request or generate/derive a compliant password hash according to the system’s guest authentication policy.
3) Create a new erp_hrm_time_tracking_guest_sessions row:
   - Set erp_hrm_time_tracking_guest_id from the active guest identity.
   - Persist ip, href, referrer.
   - Set created_at to current server timestamp.
   - Set expired_at to created_at + configured guest session TTL.
4) Return a response DTO containing the guest identity id and the issued guest session id along with relevant timestamps for client-side gating.

Transactions and consistency:
- Use a single database transaction covering guest identity lookup/creation (if needed) and session insert.
- Ensure that if any step fails, no session record is left orphaned.

Edge cases:
- If href/referrer/ip are empty or malformed according to validation rules defined in the service layer, reject.
- If concurrent requests attempt to create the same guest identity by email, handle unique constraint conflicts by re-reading after insert failure and then proceeding to session insert for the now-present identity.

Authorization:
- This operation is accessible to unauthenticated guests only; it does not require an organization-selected context. It must not perform any organization-scoped authorization checks.

responseBody.description: Guest identity/session correlation details used to gate subsequent protected requests for this unauthenticated visitor.

requestBody.description: Guest session upsert payload containing guest identity correlation and connection context metadata to issue a guest session with an expiration timestamp.

operations.description:
Retrieves a list of guest identity records that represent unauthenticated access attempts.

This operation is accessible to the guest actor (unauthenticated visitor) and returns only non-sensitive identity metadata. Guest accounts are represented in the `erp_hrm_time_tracking_guests` table, which stores a unique `email` for correlation and lifecycle timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`). The table also contains authentication-related data (`password_hash`) and an activity flag (`deleted_at`), but those fields must not be exposed to API consumers through this read operation.

The returned data is used only for identity correlation and administrative visibility patterns; it does not grant access to any organization-scoped resources. According to the guest-to-authenticated flow, any protected organization-scoped operations remain unreachable until a successful authentication establishes an authenticated session and the user selects an organization context.

Behavioral notes:
- The operation should return only active guest identity rows (where `deleted_at` is null) unless the requirements explicitly define an alternative filter; for safety, the default is to exclude deleted identities.
- Pagination/sorting should follow the service-wide list browsing expectations when the list grows large.

Related operations:
- Guest-auth entry behaviors (sign up / sign in) are handled by the authentication flow and must establish an authenticated session before any organization-scoped endpoints can be called.
operations.name: list
operations.specification:
Implement guest identity listing.

1) Authorization: allow access only for the guest actor context defined in requirements; still enforce any general authorization gates for guest browsing.
2) Query: SELECT from `erp_hrm_time_tracking_guests`.
   - Default filter: WHERE `deleted_at` IS NULL.
   - Projection: select only safe fields needed for summary DTO (id, email, created_at, updated_at).
3) Pagination: apply offset/limit or cursor-based pagination consistent with system-wide list expectations; apply sorting (e.g., newest first) if sort inputs are provided by the shared list DTO request (even if this specific operation has no request body, align with default browsing rules).
4) Response: return paginated summary type.
5) Error handling:
   - If authorization fails, return 403.
   - If no records exist, return an empty page (200).

Sensitive fields:
- Never include `password_hash` in the result payload.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of guest identity summaries (non-sensitive fields only).

operations.description:
Confirming an email address is a required onboarding step so that a member can safely continue using their account with the registered email.

This operation receives a verification token and attempts to resolve it to an existing record in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_email_verifications` (token is declared as a unique key). If the token maps to a valid, non-expired, non-invalidated verification record, the system performs the confirmation workflow: it marks the verification as no longer usable (by invalidating/removing or setting the corresponding record state as implemented by the service) and enables the associated member to be treated as having a confirmed email.

The verification token lookup is constrained by the database uniqueness rule `@@unique([token])`, and the operation must also respect the token’s lifecycle metadata: `expired_at` (must be in the future for confirmation), and `deleted_at` (records with a deletion timestamp are treated as invalid and cannot be confirmed).

Security and authorization: this endpoint is designed for unauthenticated access (guest-style confirmation). The request must not require a member session; instead, it relies exclusively on possession of the token stored in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_email_verifications.token`.

Validation rules and error handling: if the provided token does not exist, is expired, or targets a record that has been invalidated/removed (indicated by `deleted_at` being set), the system rejects the request with a clear, human-readable explanation of why completion was prevented. For rejected outcomes, the system must not create misleading success activity log entries (the verification confirmation is treated as rejected and must not masquerade as completed).

Related operations: after confirmation, the user can proceed to login using the now-confirmed email workflow already defined in the authentication requirements. If the confirmation fails, the operation leaves all persistent state unchanged for the targeted member verification outcome beyond the rejection itself.
operations.name: confirm
operations.specification:
1) Parse request body containing `token` (required) and optional `href`, `ip`, `referrer` for audit/context.

2) Database lookup (transactional read):
- Query `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_email_verifications` by `token` using the unique constraint.
- If no record found: reject with an error indicating token is invalid/not found.
- If `deleted_at` is not null: reject as invalidated.
- If `expired_at` is <= now(): reject as expired.

3) Confirmation state transition (transactional write):
- In a single transaction, invalidate the verification record according to the service’s implemented approach (e.g., set `deleted_at` and/or update `updated_at`, and/or any other mechanism the codebase uses to mark token records as invalid).
- Update the associated `member` (via the relation from `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_email_verifications.member_id`) to reflect that email is confirmed. Do not assume specific member columns unless the service layer already knows where to store verification status; Realize Agent should implement the existing mechanism.

4) Idempotency behavior:
- If the token already targets a record that is invalidated/consumed (e.g., `deleted_at` set), treat it as rejected (do not re-confirm) to avoid false positives.

5) Response mapping:
- Return the resolved verification record fields and a member summary view if the corresponding DTO is available in the codebase; otherwise return verification details only.

6) Edge cases:
- Handle race conditions where a token may be invalidated between lookup and update: re-check `deleted_at`/`expired_at` inside the transaction and reject if no longer valid.
- Ensure no partial updates: if any step fails, roll back transaction so member verification status and token invalidation remain consistent.

7) Activity logs:
- Only record an activity log entry if confirmation completed successfully.
- Never record misleading successful activity logs for rejected confirmation attempts.

responseBody.description: The verification confirmation result for the provided token, including the resolved verification record details.

requestBody.description: Email verification confirmation payload. The system uses the unique `token` to find `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_email_verifications` record and complete the email confirmation workflow.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific member email verification record by its verification identifier.

This operation reads a single row from the `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_email_verifications` table using the row primary key `id`. The returned verification record contains the token and verification context fields (including related request metadata such as IP/referrer where stored) and its lifecycle timestamps such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `expired_at`.

Access is constrained to the currently selected organization context for authenticated member actors. The service layer must ensure that the verification row is associated with a member that belongs to the selected organization before returning the data, preventing cross-organization information leakage.

This read-only endpoint is intended to support UI flows that need to display or confirm verification details after the token submission flow. It does not validate token usability or mutate any rows.

Expected behavior and error handling:
- If `verificationId` does not resolve to an accessible record within the selected organization scope, the request must fail without disclosing whether the record exists in another organization.
- On unexpected internal failures, the request fails and no partial data is returned.

Related operations may include verification creation and invalidation flows implemented elsewhere in the service; those operations produce the records this endpoint is designed to retrieve.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1) Read inputs: verificationId from path.
2) Resolve access scope:
   - Require an authenticated member actor with an active selected organization context (organization-scoped authorization).
3) Fetch verification:
   - Query `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_email_verifications` by `id = verificationId`.
4) Enforce organization isolation:
   - Join to `erp_hrm_time_tracking_members` (via `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_id`) and ensure the member belongs to the currently selected organization context.
   - If membership cannot be proven within the selected organization, reject the request.
5) Response mapping:
   - Return the verification record fields as defined by the DTO for MemberEmailVerification.
6) Error cases:
   - If not found within scope, reject with a consistent failure response (no cross-org leakage).
   - Unexpected internal errors reject without partial results.

responseBody.description: The requested member email verification record identified by verificationId.

parameters.description: Target email verification record ID (primary key) to retrieve.
parameters.name: verificationId

operations.description:
Update a member account password using a password reset token.

This operation validates the provided token identifier against the password reset records in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_password_resets`. The token identifier is used to locate the reset request row, then the system checks that the reset request has not expired via `expired_at` and has not been invalidated/hidden via `deleted_at`. If the checks fail, the system rejects the request without updating any credential fields.

If validation succeeds, this operation updates the target member's credential data in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_members`. The write performed by this endpoint is the password credential update (implemented by setting a new hashed value in `password_hash`), while the member identity and email remain unchanged.

Security and validation rules are strict: the system must not apply partial updates. If any business constraint fails (for example, token is invalid or expired, or the new password fails credential validation defined elsewhere in the service layer), the system rejects the request and leaves `erp_hrm_time_tracking_members.password_hash` unchanged. Error responses should provide a clear, human-readable explanation of what prevented completion without exposing sensitive tenant-scoped or token-internal details.

After a successful password update, the member can authenticate again using the updated password. Any subsequent session behavior is handled by the existing authentication/session rules, while this endpoint itself is responsible only for the credential update driven by the reset token.

Related operations: password change for an authenticated user is handled by the dedicated password change operation (separate from reset-token verification), and password reset initiation/token issuing is represented by other self-service flows that create rows in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_password_resets`.
operations.name: updatePasswordWithResetToken
operations.specification:
1) Parse request body payload into fields: tokenIdentifier and newPassword (and any additional flags present in the request DTO).
2) Look up reset request row in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_password_resets` by `token_identifier`.
   - If no row exists, reject with a business validation error (invalid token).
   - If `deleted_at` is not null, reject (token invalidated).
   - If current time is after `expired_at`, reject (token expired).
3) Resolve the associated member via `member_id` relation.
4) Validate the new password using the same password-credential constraints used by the normal password change flow (handled in service layer). If invalid, reject without any DB change.
5) In a single transaction:
   - Update `erp_hrm_time_tracking_members.password_hash` for the member.
   - Optionally invalidate the reset request (implementation decision): if the platform design expects tokens to be single-use, set `deleted_at` on the reset row; otherwise keep it unchanged. This must be consistent with the broader reset-token lifecycle.
6) If any step fails, rollback and ensure no partial changes.
7) Return a success response body consistent with IErpHrmTimeTrackingMember.ISummary.

Edge cases:
- Race condition: if token is invalidated or expires between lookup and update, re-check `deleted_at`/`expired_at` within the transaction before updating.
- Do not create or modify activity log entries in failure cases that represent business rejection; only add logs for successful credential updates per the system’s activity logging rules (if implemented at service-layer).

responseBody.description: Updated member summary after a successful password reset.

requestBody.description: Password reset verification request including the reset token identifier and the new password to set.

operations.description:
Retrieve a password reset request record by its identifier for password reset verification flows.

This endpoint is backed by the `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_password_resets` table, which stores the reset request row identified by `id` (UUID). Each row records the owning member (`member_id`), the opaque token lookup value embedded in the reset link/code (`token_identifier`), the expiration timestamp (`expired_at`), and bookkeeping timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`). The table also includes an optional `deleted_at` timestamp to hide invalidated/expired reset requests from normal verification lookups while preserving auditability.

Security and privacy considerations: this operation must never expose a member’s credential data and should restrict which fields are returned. It is intended to support verification logic by allowing the server to check `expired_at` and whether `deleted_at` is set. Although the database stores `token_identifier`, callers of this API should only receive the minimal information required for the verification flow; in particular, the sensitive token lookup value should be protected according to the service’s authorization model.

Validation and behavior: when `resetId` does not match any existing row, the operation should reject the request with an appropriate not-found style error. When a matching row is found, the server should interpret `expired_at` to determine whether the token is still valid, and interpret `deleted_at` (if present) to prevent verification of invalidated entries.

Relationship to other operations: this endpoint is typically used together with the reset issuance flow (the operation that creates a new row with a `token_identifier`) and the reset completion flow (the operation that validates the token and updates the member password). This endpoint enables the server-side part of token verification by returning the relevant row state required to decide whether the reset can proceed.

Error handling consistency: if verification cannot proceed due to business constraints (missing record, already expired, or invalidated via `deleted_at`), the operation must return a clear, human-readable explanation without exposing sensitive organization data or unrelated member information. Unexpected internal failures must not create misleading activity log entries or partially apply changes, and any rejected verification attempt must leave reset state unchanged.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:
1) Authenticate request per global auth rules for the service (member/guest boundaries) and enforce any authorization gating required by the verification flow.
2) Parse `resetId` from the path and treat it as UUID.
3) Query `erp_hrm_time_tracking_member_password_resets` by `id = resetId`.
4) If no row exists, throw a not-found rejection.
5) If `deleted_at` is not null, reject as invalidated.
6) Compare current time to `expired_at`; if `expired_at` is in the past, reject as expired.
7) Return a DTO containing only verification-relevant fields. Prefer excluding `token_identifier` from the response if the system design expects token secrecy; include `id` and expiry status information as required by the corresponding response DTO.

Data access details:
- Use a single-row select; no transaction is required because this is a read.
- Ensure organization isolation by relying on member ownership checks in higher layers if the service requires it.

Edge cases:
- If timestamps are present but nullability rules differ, treat missing `expired_at` as invalid and reject.
- Do not log verification failures as successful events in any activity log; only successful password changes should produce stateful audit entries.

operations.description:
Update the currently selected organization’s profile and configuration settings.

This operation targets the organization tenant boundary represented by `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations`. It updates the human-facing and configuration fields used across the ERP HRM time tracking service, including the organization display `name`, `description`, optional `logo_url`, and operational time settings such as `timezone` and `fiscal_start_month`. It also updates the organization’s `currency_code` used for financial framing and payroll-related calculations.

Security and authorization are enforced using the selected organization context. When a member belongs to multiple organizations, the system applies the requested update only within the currently selected organization context and denies any cross-organization attempt. If no organization context is selected, the system rejects the request without returning any organization data.

The operation must validate that `name` remains unique across all organizations (as required by `@@unique([name])` on `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations`). It must also validate the formats/constraints of the updated configuration values (e.g., `timezone` must be a valid IANA timezone string and `currency_code` must be a supported currency code) before persisting changes.

Timestamps: `created_at` is not updated by this operation. The database automatically tracks changes via `updated_at`; the implementation should persist updated timestamps consistently. The `deleted_at` column indicates organization deletion state; this operation should not re-activate a deleted organization unless explicitly supported by business rules.

Related operations: use organization read/list operations (if available in the API) to browse organization information before applying changes. Cross-organization switching behavior ensures that after a successful update, subsequent operations use the newly stored configuration within the same selected organization context.

Expected errors include authorization failures due to cross-organization isolation, validation failures for uniqueness (`name`) and invalid configuration values, and generic internal failures that reject without partial updates.
operations.name: updateOrganization

1) Authorization & context

3) Persistence

- Update `updated_at` automatically (or explicitly if ORM requires).
- Do not modify `id`, `created_at`.
- If `deleted_at` is non-null, reject or deny updates per domain rules (no assumption: implement according to domain error handling conventions).

4) Transactionality
- Run uniqueness check and update within a transaction or with a database constraint so race conditions cannot create duplicates.
- If uniqueness or validation fails, reject and ensure no fields are partially updated.

5) Response mapping
- Return the updated organization entity as `IErpHrmTimeTrackingOrganization` mapped from the updated row.

If no organization context is available for the user or the target organization is not accessible in the current context, the request must be rejected without disclosing identifying details from other organizations.

The response maps directly to the `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations` table fields, including the organization’s branding and financial/time framing configuration (e.g., `logo_url`, `currency_code`, `timezone`, and `fiscal_start_month`).

operations.description:
Create a new time-tracking tenant organization.

This operation creates a new row in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations`, which is the tenant boundary for all HRM time tracking data. The created organization’s configuration fields (such as `timezone`, `currency_code`, and `fiscal_start_month`) are used by downstream features to interpret dates and present tenant-specific settings.

The request payload maps to the core organization profile fields:
- `name` is the human-friendly organization name and is required.
- `description` provides an internal/contextual description.
- `logo_url` is optional branding media URL.
- `currency_code` provides the tenant’s financial framing.
- `timezone` is an IANA timezone identifier used to interpret date/time values.
- `fiscal_start_month` defines the organization’s fiscal period starting month (1-12 as an integer).

After successful creation, the response returns the created organization record including the primary key `id` (UUID) and timestamps such as `created_at`/`updated_at`. `deleted_at` is a lifecycle column managed by the system; it is not supplied by the client.

Authorization and tenant isolation: only authorized platform users should be allowed to create organizations. The service must enforce the platform’s authentication/authorization rules before performing the insert.

Validation and error handling: the implementation must validate that `name` is unique (schema requires `@@unique([name])`) and must reject requests that would violate that constraint. Unexpected internal failures must not partially write data.

Related operations: after creating an organization, clients typically create organization-scoped entities (employees, departments, contracts, projects, timelogs, timesheets, timer sessions, and reports) using their respective endpoints scoped to the organization context.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implement POST /organizations to create a new tenant organization.

Algorithm / Service-layer steps:
1. Authenticate the caller via existing auth middleware and authorize them to perform tenant creation.
2. Validate request fields against `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations` columns:
   - `name`: required; must be unique (check `@@unique([name])`).
   - `description`: required.
   - `logo_url`: optional; accept null/undefined per request DTO; store as nullable in DB.
   - `currency_code`: required.
   - `timezone`: required; store as provided (string).
   - `fiscal_start_month`: required integer; store as provided.
3. Execute an INSERT into `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations`:
   - `created_at` and `updated_at` are set by DB defaults/triggers (or set by service if DB doesn’t).
   - Ensure `deleted_at` is left NULL for newly created organizations.
4. Return the persisted organization row.

Database operations:
- Single transaction for the insert.
- Uniqueness violation handling:
  - If insertion fails due to unique constraint on `name`, return a deterministic client error (e.g., conflict) without leaking other tenant identifiers.

Edge cases:
- If `logo_url` is provided, validate it as a string URL format at the DTO layer if the DTO includes such validation; otherwise persist.
- Timezone values are stored as-is; downstream date interpretation should rely on the stored IANA timezone.

Error handling:
- On unique constraint failure for `name`, respond with a conflict-style error.
- On validation errors, respond with a bad-request style error.
- On unexpected errors, respond with a generic internal error and do not retry blindly.

Update the current organization (tenant) profile identified by the given `organizationId`.

This operation modifies organization configuration fields stored in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations`, including the organization’s display name (`name`), description (`description`), branding (`logo_url`), financial framing (`currency_code`), timezone interpretation (`timezone`), and fiscal framing (`fiscal_start_month`). The table also records audit timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`) which must be updated appropriately when changes are applied.

Security and authorization: only an authorized platform user who has management capability for the target tenant should be allowed to update this organization. In multi-organization scenarios, the selected organization context must not allow cross-organization profile edits; the implementation must ensure the caller can manage the organization identified by `organizationId`.

Validation rules and constraints: the `name` field is unique in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations` (`@@unique([name])`), so the implementation must reject updates that would cause a uniqueness conflict. `fiscal_start_month` must be a valid month number for the organization (1–12). `timezone` must be a valid IANA timezone identifier string used to interpret date/time values for that tenant. `logo_url` is optional and, when provided, should be a valid URL. `currency_code` is required and is stored as a string used for organization financial framing.

Record state: `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations` includes `deleted_at` for tenant deletion state. If `deleted_at` is non-null for the target organization, the implementation must not allow normal updates; return an authorization/state error indicating the organization is unavailable.

Related operations: after updating the organization profile, clients commonly re-fetch the organization details using the corresponding read operation (not defined here) to confirm the persisted values and server-calculated timestamps.

operations.specification:
Implement PUT /organizations/{organizationId}.

1) Authorization and scope
- Verify the caller has permission to manage the target organization identified by `organizationId`.
- Enforce tenant isolation: never allow updating any organization other than the one identified by the path parameter.

2) Input validation
- Validate request body fields map to columns in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations`:
  - name, description, logo_url, currency_code, timezone, fiscal_start_month.
- Enforce `name` uniqueness constraint (organization table has @@unique([name])). If conflict occurs, raise a validation error.
- Validate fiscal_start_month is within 1..12.
- Validate timezone string is non-empty and conforms to IANA timezone naming expectations (implementation may rely on a timezone library).
- Validate logo_url, if provided, is a syntactically valid URL.

3) Fetch and state checks
- Load the target organization row by `id`.
- If not found, return not-found error.
- If deleted_at is non-null, reject the update as organization is unavailable.

4) Persistence
- In a transaction, apply updates to the loaded row.
- Update updated_at to current timestamp.
- created_at must remain unchanged.

5) Response
- Return the updated organization resource as the response body.

Error handling
- Map uniqueness conflicts (name) to a clear client error.
- Map invalid input to request validation errors.
- Map missing/disabled tenant state to not-found or unavailable-state errors consistently.

operations.description:
Permanently removes an organization record identified by `organizationId`.

This endpoint operates on the tenant boundary represented by the `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations` table. The organization contains tenant-scoped configuration fields such as `name`, `description`, `logo_url`, `currency_code`, `timezone`, and `fiscal_start_month`, and it is referenced as the root parent for organization-scoped entities (employees, departments, projects, timelogs, timesheets, and reports) via foreign keys.

Security and authorization: access must be limited to authorized actors in the context of the targeted organization. The implementation must ensure the caller is operating within the correct organization scope and is permitted to perform the deletion.

Validation and business rules: before removing the organization record, the service layer must enforce organization lifecycle constraints and dependency preconditions described in the requirements (e.g., pending workflow and ownership-related constraints as applicable to organization deletion). If any precondition is not satisfied, the request must be rejected with an appropriate error response.

Error handling: if `organizationId` does not exist, or the caller has no permission for that organization, the operation must return an error response. If preconditions fail, the operation must not remove the organization.

Related operations: clients typically call an organization retrieval endpoint first to confirm the target `organizationId`, and may call listing/search operations to discover organizations available in the user’s organization context before attempting deletion.

1) Authorization & scope
- Verify the caller is authenticated as a `member` (and/or admin as defined by your permission model) and has the right to delete the targeted organization.

2) Input handling

4) Deletion transaction
- Start a database transaction.
- Delete the organization row in `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organizations` where `id = organizationId`.
- Ensure cascading behavior (or explicit deletes) for all organization-scoped dependent entities is consistent with the database schema and required retention policy.
- Commit the transaction.

5) Audit/recording (if required by the system)
- If the requirements specify audit logging for deletion, write an activity log entry with the acting user and the targeted entity.

6) Success response

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of departments for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint supports department browsing within an organization-scoped HR structure, reflecting the department hierarchy that employees and organization managers manage. The returned list is derived from the erp_hrm_time_tracking_departments table, which stores each department’s organization ownership (erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id), optional parent department reference (parent_department_id), display name (name), and free-text description (description).

Security and authorization are applied at execution time: while operating in a selected organization context, all department operations must apply only to the data of that organization, preventing cross-organization access if the context does not match the target department’s organization. Requests from users who are not properly authorized for department browsing still must not reveal other organizations’ department data.

Filtering behavior is designed for UI list browsing. The operation accepts search criteria (e.g., name keyword) and supports pagination and sorting. When the selected organization has no departments, the system must return an empty list state scoped to that organization (and must not error or fabricate placeholder departments).

Returned department summary items should include the department identifiers and core display fields needed for list rendering, while avoiding unnecessary nested data. Hierarchy information (such as the presence of a parent department) may be included in summary form, based on what the corresponding ISummary DTO exposes.

Related operations: administrators can modify individual department details using the department edit APIs, and users can view the department list using this operation as their primary browsing mechanism. If a user edits a department, subsequent calls to this endpoint must reflect the latest name/description values for that organization.
operations.name: index

Implement PATCH /departments as a list/search over erp_hrm_time_tracking_departments.

1) Resolve organization scope from the authenticated member’s currently selected organization context.
   - All queries must filter by erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = selectedOrganizationId.

2) Apply deletion handling per schema: only include active rows (deleted_at IS NULL).

3) Apply request search filters:
   - Use request DTO fields (IErpHrmTimeTrackingDepartment.IRequest) for keyword matching on name and optional filtering on parent_department_id and description if present.

4) Pagination and sorting:
   - Apply pagination and sorting from the request DTO.

5) Mapping:
   - Map database rows to IErpHrmTimeTrackingDepartment.ISummary (or the exact generated type corresponding to that name variant) including id, name, description (if included in ISummary), parent_department_id (if included in ISummary), and timestamps as available.

6) Edge cases:
   - If there are no matching departments, return an empty page.
   - Validate any provided parent_department_id filter is treated as a filter only (no cross-org resolution/validation should be attempted in a list call).

7) Transactionality:
   - No write operations; no transaction required beyond consistent read.

8) Error handling:
   - If organization context is missing/invalid per auth middleware, reject accordingly (handled upstream). For this operation, rely on auth layer to guarantee a valid selected organization context.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single department record by its identifier within the currently selected organization context.

This operation returns the department’s core profile fields used by the UI and business logic: the department name and optional description. Because departments are organized hierarchically, the response also supports the optional parent-department relationship, enabling clients to render nested department structures (one level of nesting) inside the same organization.

Authorization and context are enforced via the selected organization scope: every department belongs to exactly one organization, and this endpoint must prevent cross-organization access. If the authenticated member does not have access to the currently selected organization, or if the requested department belongs to a different organization than the active context, the system must reject the request.

The underlying database model stores the department’s organization id (erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id), name, optional parent_department_id, and a deleted_at timestamp. The operation must therefore only return records that are valid for the active browsing context; records marked as deleted must not be returned as active department details.

Clients typically pair this operation with the department list browsing endpoint to allow users to select a department and then view its details. For editing or deletion, dedicated write operations are expected to be used instead of this read endpoint.

2) Resolve the active organization context for the authenticated member (the organization selected by the user in the current session/context).

   - id
   - name
   - description (nullable)
   - parentDepartmentId (nullable; derived from parent_department_id)

8) Optionally (if DTO includes parent summary fields) join parent department to include its id and name; do not expand grandchildren beyond what the DTO supports.

9) No database transaction is required (read-only).

operations.description:
Create a new department within the currently selected organization.

This operation allows an authorized member to create an organizational unit used to organize employees inside the selected organization context. A department requires a name and may optionally include a description. The department can also optionally reference a parent department to form a small hierarchy (the system supports only the allowed nesting depth).

While handling the request, the system enforces organization context isolation: when creating a department, the department (and any referenced parent department) must belong to the member’s currently selected organization. If a provided parent department belongs to a different organization, the create request is rejected to prevent cross-organization access.

The system also validates structural correctness for the parent relationship. If the requested parent assignment would produce an invalid hierarchy depth/shape, the system rejects the operation and leaves department data unchanged.

Permissions: department creation is restricted to users who have the organization management authority within the currently selected organization (org:manage). Users without that capability are denied.

After successful creation, the newly created department becomes immediately available in the organization’s department list so subsequent department filtering and list browsing reflect the updated structure.

Related usage: clients typically call the departments list/read endpoint to display available departments; right after this create call succeeds, the new department should appear there.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation steps for creating a department:

1) Authorization & context
- Resolve the current organization context from the authenticated member/session (selected organization).
- Verify the caller has the organization management permission (org:manage) for that selected organization.
- Enforce context isolation: the created department must use erp_hrm_time_tracking_departments.erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = selectedOrganization.id.

2) Validate request payload
- Validate required fields for the Department create request DTO (name required; description optional; parent_department_id optional).
- If parent_department_id is provided:
  - Load the parent department by id.
  - Ensure parent.erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id == selectedOrganization.id. If not, reject the request.
  - Validate nesting depth constraint: detect whether linking this department to the parent would create an invalid parent structure (more than one nesting level as defined by requirements). If invalid, reject the request.

3) Uniqueness within organization
- Enforce the database unique constraint: @@unique([erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id, name]).
- If another non-deleted department in the same organization already has the same name, reject with an appropriate validation error.

4) Create transaction
- In a transaction, insert into erp_hrm_time_tracking_departments:
  - id: generated UUID by the database/ORM.
  - erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id: selectedOrganization.id.
  - parent_department_id: request.parent_department_id or null.
  - name: request.name.
  - description: request.description.
  - created_at / updated_at: set by server/ORM.
  - deleted_at: set to null on creation.

5) Response
- Return the created department mapped to IErpHrmTimeTrackingDepartment.
- Ensure timestamps and resolved parent references (if any) are consistent with what was stored.

Edge cases
- Parent id provided but not found: reject.
- Parent belongs to different organization: reject.
- Invalid nesting scenario: reject without inserting.
- Name uniqueness conflict within the same organization: reject.

operations.description:
Update a department within the currently selected organization context.

This operation modifies the persisted data for a single department identified by `departmentId`, including its required `name` and optional `description`, and it may also change the department’s optional `parent_department_id` to adjust the one-level hierarchy inside the same organization. Departments are organization-scoped: every department record belongs to exactly one organization via `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id`, so the update must never cross organization boundaries.

The system must enforce organization-scoped access during the update. While operating in a selected organization context, the system applies department operations only to the data of that organization, preventing attempts to update a department using a mismatched context.

Hierarchy validation is required when changing the parent relationship. A department may reference an optional parent department via `parent_department_id` only within the same organization. The system must detect invalid parent structures during creation and editing; an invalid parent structure includes any attempt that would result in more than one level of nesting when interpreted across the referenced departments. If such an invalid parent structure is detected, the system rejects the change and leaves the existing department data unchanged.

Time fields are maintained by the persistence layer. The department table includes `created_at` and `updated_at`; this operation updates `updated_at` to reflect the modification time while preserving `created_at`.

This operation is intended to be used alongside:
- The department list browsing operation to discover department ids and current hierarchy for the selected organization.
- The department detail retrieval operation to view a department before editing its `name`, `description`, or parent assignment.

On success, this endpoint returns the updated department entity. On validation failures (e.g., parent department from a different organization, or invalid nesting depth), the system rejects the request without partially applying changes.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1) Authorization & context validation
- Resolve the requesting actor and ensure the operation is permitted to manage departments in the currently selected organization context (org:manage as specified for department write permissions).
- Load target department by id from `erp_hrm_time_tracking_departments`.
- Verify the loaded department’s `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id` equals the selected organization id from the session/context. If mismatch, reject to prevent cross-organization access.

2) Input validation
- Validate request body fields against schema expectations:
  - `name` is required (non-empty as enforced by DTO validation layer).
  - `description` may be null/omitted in DTO (maps to nullable `description` column).
  - `parentDepartmentId` (if provided) maps to `parent_department_id`.
- If `parent_department_id` is provided/changed:
  - If it is non-null, load the referenced parent department and verify it belongs to the same organization (`erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id`). Reject if not.
  - Enforce one-level nesting: verify that the target parent does not have a parent of its own (i.e., proposed parent must not create nesting deeper than one level). Reject the update if it would cause more than one level of nesting.
  - Reject any scenario that represents an invalid parent structure per the requirements; apply no partial changes.

3) Transaction and persistence
- Begin transaction.
- Apply updates to `erp_hrm_time_tracking_departments`:
  - Set `name`, `description` (nullable), and `parent_department_id` (nullable) according to request.
  - Update `updated_at` to current time.
  - Do not alter `created_at`.
- Commit transaction.

4) Activity/audit integration (if applicable)
- If the service records activity log entries for department edits, create an `erp_hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_entries` record referencing the updated department and performed-by user. (If no such cross-cutting logging exists in implementation, skip.)

5) Response
- Return the updated department entity after persistence, including its id, organization id, optional parent department id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at state as defined by the department DTO.

6) Edge cases
- If the department id does not exist, return not-found.
- If the parent change fails validation (wrong organization or invalid nesting depth), return a validation error and ensure the original department remains unchanged.
- Ensure that attempting to update a record that is already marked deleted (non-null `deleted_at`) follows the service’s existing behavior; if such behavior is not defined, treat it as not-found or reject consistently with other department operations.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a department from the currently selected organization.

This operation deletes the target `erp_hrm_time_tracking_departments` record that belongs to the authenticated member’s currently selected organization context. When a department is removed from an organization’s structure, the system preserves employees by clearing their department reference (employees’ department association is set to `null`) instead of deleting employee records.

The operation enforces organization-scoped authorization: only a user with organization management authority for the currently selected organization may perform department deletion. If the department does not exist within the selected organization context, or the caller lacks authority, the system rejects the request without changing any department or employee data.

After successful deletion, the deleted department must no longer appear in the department list for that organization, and its details must not be retrievable. Employees remain available in the employee directory per their current assignment state; the only change is that the department information for employees previously assigned to the deleted department is no longer present.

This behavior is defined by the department deletion requirements: deletion clears employee department assignments, preserves employee historical employment identity and all related time data (timelogs and timesheets), and does not remove projects, tasks, or their time records.

Related operations: combine with the departments list and employee views to confirm that the department is filtered out and that affected employees now show a `null` department assignment.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1) Authorization & scope
- Resolve current organization context from the authenticated member/session.
- Verify caller has organization owner authority to manage organization data in the selected organization context (owner-only authority for department create/edit/delete).
- If the caller lacks permission, reject with an authorization/permission error before any DB changes.

2) Validate target department
- Load the department row by `id = departmentId` from `erp_hrm_time_tracking_departments`.
- If not found, reject with not-found (no DB modifications).
- Ensure the loaded department’s `erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id` matches the current organization context. If it does not match, reject (do not disclose cross-tenant existence).

3) Transactional deletion + employee reference clearing
- Start a DB transaction.
- Delete the department row from `erp_hrm_time_tracking_departments`.
- Clear department assignment for all employees currently referencing the deleted department:
  - Update the employees table to set the employees’ department reference column to `null` for rows where their department reference equals the deleted department id.
  - This must happen within the same transaction to avoid leaving employees in a broken state.
- Commit the transaction.

4) Post-conditions
- Department list endpoints must no longer return the deleted department for this organization.
- Employees remain in the organization and remain visible in employee directory views; their department association is now null.

5) Edge cases
- If there are no employees referencing the department, deletion still succeeds.
- Never delete or cascade into employee records; ensure only the employee department reference is cleared.
- Never partially apply: if any step fails, roll back the transaction so employee references and department data remain consistent.

6) Activity/audit integration (if present in the service layer)
- Optionally record an organization-scoped activity log entry capturing that a department was erased, including the acting user, timestamp, and target entity id/type. This must not affect the deletion outcome if the logging mechanism is best-effort.

parameters.description: The UUID identifier of the department to permanently remove within the currently selected organization context.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of employment contracts for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint is designed for contract browsing use cases such as viewing active and historical employment agreement records within the selected organization context.

The underlying data comes from {@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts}, which stores organization-scoped contract attributes including {@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts.contract_number}, {@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts.contract_title}, pay terms ({@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts.pay_amount}, {@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts.pay_currency}, {@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts.pay_frequency}), working-term dates ({@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts.work_term_start_date}, {@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts.work_term_end_date}), and lifecycle {@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts.status}.

This operation must ensure strict tenant isolation by filtering results with {@link erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts.erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id} derived from the selected organization context, preventing any records from other organizations from being returned.

Filtering and sorting are provided via the request body because the endpoint uses HTTP PATCH for complex query criteria. Returned items are list-safe summaries and do not perform updates; contract immutability rules for past agreements are enforced by write operations, not by this list operation.

If no contracts match the criteria, return an empty paginated result while keeping the pagination metadata consistent.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a read-only list/search operation for contracts.

1) Resolve tenant scope:
- Determine selected organization id from request context (organization context middleware).
- Build a base query on erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts where erp_hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = selectedOrgId.

2) Apply record visibility rules:
- Exclude logically retired contracts by default (deleted_at IS NULL) unless the IRequest supports including deleted records; if such a flag exists in IRequest, apply it.

3) Apply filtering from IErpHrmTimeTrackingContract.IRequest:
- Filter by contract_number and/or contract_title.
- Filter by status.
- Filter by work_term_start_date and work_term_end_date ranges.
- If the request includes employee-related filters, ensure any referenced employees are within the same selected organization (via erp_hrm_time_tracking_employee_id membership relation) and are viewable by the caller per service authorization.

4) Apply sorting:
- Map allowed sort keys from IRequest to actual columns in erp_hrm_time_tracking_contracts (e.g., created_at, work_term_start_date, work_term_end_date, status).
- Use a deterministic secondary sort (e.g., created_at then id) to keep pagination stable.

5) Pagination:
- Apply pagination strategy consistent with IRequest (page/limit or cursor-based).
- Fetch only the columns needed for IPageIErpHrmTimeTrackingContract.ISummary.

6) Authorization:
- Verify at service layer that the caller is allowed to view contract results for the employee scope implied by the filters.
- Never broaden scope beyond selected organization.

7) Error handling:
- Invalid filter combinations or invalid pagination parameters should return a validation error.
- If organization context is missing/invalid, return an authorization/tenant scoping error.

8) Transactions:
- No mutation. Run as read-only.

Implementation details should use ORM query builder with parameterized inputs.
